When my team researched your work, we discovered perhaps the world's most unusual restaurant - your langar.(Laughs) Well, Sanjiv, we certainly haven't had a “reservations desk” in our langar for the last 3 decades! The reason is simple: hunger doesn't make appointmentsAnyone can come to my home and receive food. No application. No appointment. No eligibility test! To me, it is one of the most natural and satisfying things to do.You have experienced wealth and yet you say that your langar gives you a satisfaction no amount of wealth can buy. Isn't this a paradox?Only if we assume that everything valuable has a price! (Laughs). A meal has a price. A blessing doesn't come with a price tag! Sanjiv, I don't really think of myself as giving anything. I am simply sharing my abundance. Service comes naturally to me. It is my joy. That is why I often say to myself: Feed. Feed. Feed.You make feeding sound almost spiritual. Is that why Annapurna resonates so strongly with your philosophy?Annapurna represents something beautiful in our tradition - the assurance that nobody should remain hungry. To me, that also means responsibility. If the Universe has been generous to us, surely, we can share that abundance with others?Take a hospital, for example. While doctors care for patients, who looks after their families? That is what led me to become involved in pioneering community kitchens serving patients' families outside AIIMS (All India Institute of Medical Sciences), New Delhi.And how did water become part of your mission?: (Laughs) Sanjiv, when someone is thirsty in 45-degree heat, they don't need a lecture on climate change. They need a glass of cool water!When the Delhi Heat Action Plan was launched by the Chief Minister. Rekha Gupta, I was delighted to be invited by Rajendra Singh of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, to support the initiative through digital cool-water dispensing machines. Impact doesn't have to be glamorous. It has to be useful!Could your philosophy ofhelp bridge the rural -urban divide?Absolutely! The people constructing and maintaining our homes and cities often come from distant villages.As fellow Bharatwasis, isn't it our responsibility to ensure that they receive fresh, nutritious food, are paid generously for their services and are treated with dignity?And I mean proper nutrition - wholesome, preferably home-cooked food prepared with good ingredients and healthy oils.Think of a migrant worker who has come to a city to earn a livelihood but has no kitchen of his own. If we provide him with fresh, nutritious food, he not only stays healthier but can also save more of his hard-earned income. And where do those savings go? Back to his family in the village! That money flows into rural Bharat, supporting families, strengthening local businesses and, as it circulates through village economies, potentially contributing to better housing, facilities and infrastructure.Our cities have infrastructure that many of our villages still lack. What if we could help bridge that gap through something as simple as sharing nutritious food? Every migrant worker is a human bridge between rural and urban Bharat. If we strengthen that bridge, we strengthen Bharat itself!And Sanjiv, life is a mirror. When we help others grow, we grow too.That is why I believecan become something much larger than a meal.That sounds like a much bigger idea than feeding people. Are you suggesting that Anna is also about how we treat one another?Precisely! Anna begins with food, but it cannot end there. What good is a meal if we deny someone dignity? We must recognise that the people who serve us are our fellow Bharatiyas. Their nutrition, welfare and dignity should matter to us. Pay them generously. Feed them nutritiously. Treat them respectfully, with dignityI find the thinking of Nobel Laureate and Harvard University Professor Amartya Sen particularly profound: development is not merely about rising incomes, but about expanding people's real freedoms - including the freedom to live without hunger. After all, what meaning does prosperity have if people are still denied the basic dignity of a nutritious meal?But isn't hunger fundamentally the government's responsibility?A government can create a food-security system. Citizens help create a culture in which nobody's hunger is ignored. I believe that caring for our fellow citizens is a personal responsibility, not merely an act of generosity. It is a moral commitment. That is the Bharat I would love to see. I believe we need to rediscover a very personal relationship with our country. Every morning, why not ask ourselves one little question: What can I do today to make my Bharat a little better?But how do we turn that sentiment into something practical?(Laughs) Ah, Sanjiv! We Bharatiyas are very good at slogans. Sometimes we need to be equally good at acting upon them!Let us start with a small deed, not a big program:Each one, feed one!Finally, how does Anna fit into your larger vision of Viksit Bharat 2047?Sanjiv, along with economic growth, technology and global influence, we must nourish our workers and our future generations. A well-nourished Bharat is the foundation of a Viksit Bharat.I have always loved the writings of Ralph Waldo Emerson. One thought I draw from his philosophy is that when we hold a powerful vision and act upon it with conviction, the world around us can begin to move in that direction. I believe that when we send a thought of goodness into the Universe, and follow it with action, we help make that goodness a reality. I dream of a healthy nation.Four hundred cities. Sixteen thousand villages. Millions of lives touched by one simple idea: Each One, Feed One! That is my dream for Bharat. And Sanjiv, I can see it happening!You may possess the Kohinoor, but what good will it do you when it cannot give you a blessing? Feed a hungry person, and you will definitely receive a blessing that no diamond can ever give.(Laughs) So my message is simple: Live consciously. Look beyond yourself. Each one, feed one.
Article Summary: Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, talks to Aruna Lohia Goenka about her YASHA framework for India. The framework includes Shiksha (education), Yuva (youth), Hunar (skills) and Abundance (shared prosperity) Share your thoughts in the comments.

Article Title: PM Modi pays tribute to former PM Indira Gandhi on birth anniversary
Article Text:
On the occasion of Indira Gandhi's birth anniversary, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar paid tribute to her legacy.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday paid tribute to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary, remembering her contributions to the country.Taking to X, PM shared a brief message marking the occasion. "Paying tribute to former Prime Minister Smt. Indira Gandhi Ji on her birth anniversary," he posted.Several Congress leaders, including Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and party president Mallikarjun Kharge, also remembered the country's first and only woman prime minister.Rahul Gandhi paid tribute to his grandmother by sharing a conversation between his mother, Sonia Gandhi, and sister, Priyanka, about Indira Gandhi.He wrote on X: "Dadi was formidable: fearless, resilient, and full of love. Her strength lives on in the women of my family, each one unique and brilliant in her own way. Their love and warmth hold us together, and they inspire me every single day.""Happy birthday, Dadi. You would be so proud of them," he added.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also paid tribute to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary, describing her as a "tigress" and saying there would never be another leader like her.“Happy Birthday, tigress! There will never be another like you,” Priyanka Gandhi posted on X.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi and other senior leaders also paid floral tributes to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary at the central hall of Samvidhan Sadan in New Delhi. Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar also marked the occasion with a tribute, describing Indira Gandhi as the “Iron Lady”. He highlighted her role in shaping India's political and economic landscape during her years in office.In his message on X, the Karnataka chief minister pointed to her contributions to agriculture, banking and the country's space and nuclear programmes. He said her tenure saw several major developments that influenced India's growth.Shivakumar added that PM Indira Gandhi continued to hold an important place in the country's post-independence history. He said her contribution to India's political journey and development would be remembered with respect.The tributes came as the country marked the birth anniversary of one of India's most prominent political leaders, Indira Gandhi, who was born on November 19, 1917, in Allahabad, now Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh and the daughter of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru. She made history as the country's first woman Prime Minister.Former PM Indira Gandhi held the top office from 1966 to 1977 and returned for a second term in 1980. She served until her assassination in 1984. Her son, Rajiv Gandhi, took over as Prime Minister after her death.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar paid tribute to her legacy. Congress leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and party president Mallikarjun Kharge also remembered the country's first and only woman prime minister.

Article Title: One boundary at a time, Yashasvi Jaiswal deflates New Zealand
Article Text:
Yashasvi Jaiswal (Pic credit: BCCI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brief Scores

New Zealand 1st innings: 368 all out in 121 overs (Henry Nicholls 175, Glenn Phillips 118; Jasprit Bumrah 4/92, Akash Deep 3/53)

India 1st innings: 159 for 1 after 39 overs (Yashasvi Jaiswal 85, KL Rahul 52 batting; Matt Henry 1/43)

WELLINGTON: Straight as an arrow, Yashasvi Jaiswal smoked one past Jacob Duffy to bring up his half-century off 66 balls. Another boundary, a rare scratchy one, followed the next ball as the southpaw moved to 54 with his tenth four of the innings. India had already surpassed their previous best opening stand of 73 in this part of the world, dating back to 2009, and Jaiswal was throwing punches with sublime strokeplay.There were no half-measures. He drove beautifully, wasn't afraid to deploy the ramp and kept finding gaps with ease against New Zealand's seamers. The left-handed batter operated with a lot of assurance after giving the new ball the required respect and never looked back. There was a lot of arrogance in the way he went about his business, bordering on audacity against a potent bowling attack featuring Jacob Duffy, Kyle Jamieson and Nathan Smith.The calmness of KL Rahul at the other end was the perfect antidote as the two stitched together a fluent partnership to give India a solid start to their innings. Rahul was lucky to survive an LBW shout early in the innings, but he hardly drew attention as Jaiswal stepped on the gas. The 24-year-old hit 16 boundaries during his knock, and his intent after reaching his half-century blew the Kiwis away.The next 35 runs came off just 32 deliveries, with 28 of those runs scored in boundaries.Jacob Duffy struggled, and Jaiswal never allowed any fast bowler in the opposition camp to find rhythm. His footwork remained precise, and his shot selection was impeccable. Except for that wild hoick moments after his fifty, Jaiswal largely played on merit and operated with a watertight defence off the back foot.The youngster featured in three India A-New Zealand A fixtures before the Test series and came well prepared for the two-match series. His starts in those fixtures were subdued, but he roared back with scores of 155* and 102 and carried the confidence from those games into the Wellington opener. Jaiswal's runs and intent not only wiped off the valuable deficit but also deflated the opposition by not allowing them an opportunity to stitch together a plan.With nothing happening off the surface or in the air, and the ball losing its sheen off Jaiswal's willow, the hosts threw a desperate dice by bringing the wicketkeeper up to the opener. Not that Jaiswal was walking into his shots, but it was just an attempt to make things happen when he wasn't allowing anything to happen.The move gave the hosts their first and only success of the day as Jaiswal nicked one to Tom Blundell off Matt Henry to end his entertaining 89-ball essay. Head down, he dragged himself back to the dressing room to a roaring applause, well aware that a big score was there for the taking. His 85 helped India put 130 on the board in just 27.5 overs and could well have delivered a decisive blow to the opposition.
Article Summary: Yashasvi Jaiswal scores 85 as India reach 159-1 in their first innings. The wicketkeeper hit 16 boundaries in an entertaining 89-ball essay. New Zealand were bowled out for 368, with Henry Nicholls scoring 175.

NEW DELHI: A 12-year-old boy was killed after being run over by a bulldozer that was returning from a Samajwadi Party (SP) roadshow led by party supremo Akhilesh Yadav in Uttar Pradesh 's Gorakhpur . The SP, however, refuted all charges and claimed that the incident took place after Akhilesh's convoy had already moved past the area. The SP media cell also shared CCTV footage of the incident to back-up their claim.Former UP CM Akhilesh Yadav had received a grand 'bulldozer welcome' during his PDA 'rath yatra' in Yogi Adityanath's bastion, Gorakhpur on Wednesday.The deceased, identified as Aryavardhan Singh, was a resident of Rajdhani village in Chauri Chaura. His father is a local BJP leader. The incident took place in the Koodaghat area during the SP's Rath Yatra, officials told IANS.According to the boy's father, Omkar Singh, the bulldozer was showering flower petals on the rally when it hit his son. He alleged that Akhilesh Yadav's convoy had already moved ahead when the bulldozer, which was approaching at high speed, struck the boy from behind.Speaking to news agency IANS, Omkar Singh said, "Around 2pm, when Akhilesh Yadav's convoy passed, my son was going to pick up his sister from Kendriya Vidyalaya.While he was crossing the road, Akhilesh Yadav's convoy had moved ahead.""A flower-showering JCB was following the convoy at a very high speed so that flowers could be showered on Akhilesh Yadav from behind. During that time, my son was crossing the road when the JCB ran over him. He died on the spot," he added.The impact of the collision reportedly flung Aryavardhan towards a road divider, leaving him with a severe injury to the back of his head. He later succumbed to his injuries.The incident triggered a sharp reaction from the Uttar Pradesh BJP, which alleged negligence in the conduct of the roadshow and criticised the behaviour of SP supporters during the procession.In a statement, the UP BJP said, "In Gorakhpur, SP supporters, in their frenzy to welcome Akhilesh Yadav, took the life of an innocent 12-year-old child! The child died a painful death after being hit by a JCB during the PDA chariot procession -- the result of SP supporters' rowdiness and irresponsible behaviour.""This is what they're like while out of power; imagine the havoc they'll wreak once they come to power! Should we call them SP supporters or hooligans? Is a show of power more precious to them than an innocent child's life?" it added.An investigation into the incident is under way. Further details are awaited.Refuting the allegations, the media cell of the SP tweeted CCTV footage which it claimed showed that the child was hit by a "saffron-colored Roadways bus" after Akhilesh's convoy had already moved on from the area."The accident in Gorakhpur that the media, the BJP and the lying chief minister Adityanath are claiming was caused by a collision with a JCB, killing a child, was actually caused by a saffron-colored Roadways bus directly under the chief minister’s control. The CCTV footage clearly shows the Roadways bus hitting that child on the road," the SP said in a post on X."Since the child’s father is a BJP member, chief minister Adityanath and the BJP together got him to make a false statement and gave him and the child’s family a false account of what happened, which misled the family into starting to blame the Samajwadi Party. But the CCTV footage reveals the whole truth. Uncontrolled, dilapidated Roadways buses keep running over innocent people every day, but the chief minister, who collects the full fare, doesn’t bat an eyelid. All he has done to fulfill his responsibility is have the buses painted saffron. I don’t know how he has the nerve to stand on stage and lie. The truth is out, and the shamelessness of the chief minister and all the BJP members has been exposed. The media channels that were running false news at the BJP’s behest have also been exposed," it added.
Article Summary: A Aryavardhan Singh, 12, was killed after being run over by a bulldozer. The bulldozer was returning from a Samajwadi Party roadshow led by Akhilesh Yadav. The incident triggered a sharp reaction from the Uttar Pradesh BJP, which alleged negligence in the conduct of the roadshow.

Article Title: Noted journalist, classical vocalist Sakuntala Narasimhan dies at 86
Article Text:
Sakuntala Narasimhan died on Wednesday. (Picture Credit: X)

BENGALURU: Noted journalist, columnist and classical vocalist Sakuntala Narasimhan died here on Wednesday, sources close to her said.She was 86 and breathed her last at a care home here after battling cancer, they said.Narasimhan, a double PhD holder, worked with several leading newspapers.She was also an accomplished musician, holding the rare distinction of being equally proficient in both Hindustani and Carnatic classical music.Narasimhan also left her mark as a travel writer, music scholar, critic, and consumer rights activist.
Article Summary: Sakuntala Narasimhan, a double PhD holder, worked with several leading newspapers. She was equally proficient in both Hindustani and Carnatic classical music. She also left her mark as a travel writer, music scholar, critic, and consumer rights activist.

AMRITSAR: As Sonia Gandhi ’s memoir,, brings renewed attention to her personal journey and family history, a Sikh man has an unusual connection to her past.Sukhdev Singh Kang claims to have purchased the Maino family's ancestral home in Italy, which he says is Sonia Gandhi’s birthplace. Born on December 9, 1946, the former Congress president spent her early years in the Italian village, and Kang is now preparing to convert the six-room property into a museum dedicated to her family and early life.Located in Lusiana, a village in Italy’s Vicenza province in the Veneto region, the house has gradually emerged as a point of interest for visitors, particularly from India. Kang has put up a board outside the property identifying it as the “Indian House, Place of Birth, 9 December 1946, Sonia Gandhi”.Kang, who lives with his wife, son and daughter in Brescia, about an hour’s drive from Lusiana, said he purchased the property in 2020 but declined to disclose its price. He said the family had decided to convert it into a museum and had now obtained the necessary permissions to take the project forward. With Sonia Gandhi’s memoir drawing public attention to her personal journey, he feels this is the right time to develop the property as a museum.“We want to meet Sonia Gandhi and her children, Rahul and Priyanka, to learn more about the family’s story and understand which personal belongings and other articles could be displayed in the museum. We want visitors to get a glimpse of her family background and early life,” Kang told TOI during his visit to Amritsar on Thursday.Born into an ordinary family in Lusiana, Sonia Gandhi’s journey has been extraordinary. Kang said her father, Stefano Maino, was a mason and building contractor, and there was little in her early life to suggest that she would one day emerge as one of the most influential women in Indian politics.From a modest Italian village, she went on to marry Rajiv Gandhi, become the wife of a Prime Minister, and eventually lead the Indian National Congress, one of the world's largest political parties. Her association with the Nehru-Gandhi family placed her at the centre of one of India's most influential political dynasties, marking a remarkable journey from a small-town upbringing to the corridors of power.Kang said the family would be delighted if Sonia Gandhi and her children visited the property. “We are proud owners of Sonia Gandhi’s house. It is their family home, and we are ready to hand over the keys whenever they wish to come,” he said, adding that people known to the family in the village were also eager to meet her.Stating that over the years, the property has become a talking point among villagers, Kang said locals immediately identify it as “Sonia Gandhi’s house” whenever they see visitors from India, particularly Sikhs, understanding that they have come to see the former Congress president’s ancestral home.The growing tourist interest has also benefited the village economy, with visitors spending money at local eateries and accommodation facilities. Several prominent residents, including politicians, had attended the house’s inauguration, he said. The family also organises a function every year on Sonia Gandhi’s birthday, he added.Kang said he spends 100 euros a month on a caretaker and pays around 1,000 euros annually in property taxes. Despite suggestions from some people to rent out the house for more than 800 euros a month or convert it into a gurdwara, the family has refused.“We do not want to rent out our prized possession or change its character. We intend to preserve it as a place associated with Sonia Gandhi’s family,” he said.Asked about Sikh hardliners who hold the Gandhi family responsible for Operation Bluestar, Kang dismissed their criticism, saying only a handful of such elements were pursuing their own separatist agenda. He maintained that the operation was a decision of the government of the day and that blaming the Gandhi family personally for it was misplaced.For Kang, the property is not merely a real estate acquisition but an opportunity to preserve a small piece of the personal history of one of India's most prominent political figures.
Article Summary: Sukhdev Singh Kang claims to have purchased the Maino family's ancestral home in Italy, which he says is Sonia Gandhi’s birthplace. Born on December 9, 1946, the former Congress president spent her early years in the Italian village, and Kang is now preparing to convert the six-room property into a museum.

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday launched a broadside against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over his remarks at an event in Chicago. BJP leaders claimed that Rahul Gandhi called Indian democracy "sick". The video put out by news agencies, however, showed that he had actually described the democracy as "sacred".In a social media post on X, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari shared a clip of Rahul's address and termed him "leader of anti-India propaganda.""Rahul Gandhi called Indian Democracy 'sick' from foreign soil! Congress calls Indian democracy 'sick'. Rahul Gandhi has yet again proven he loves Parivar, & hates Democracy!" Bhandari said."Every time Rahul proves he is against Indian state, People of India & India's Democratic Fabric! Rahul Gandhi is Leader of Anti India Propaganda!" he added.Several BJP leaders also followed Bhandari in attacking Rahul, saying that the Congress leader was "moving towards senile mental dementia.""Rahul Gandhi himself is sick; he has been unwell for 10 years. He has developed an illness called obsessive-compulsive neurosis for the past 10 years, and now he is gradually moving towards senile mental dementia," BJP spokesperson Ajay Alok said."He has become incoherent. Look at him - he has no sense of place, time, or object. He thinks one thing in his mind, and something else comes out of his mouth. What was he even trying to say? Saying about his own mother that at every mile, Mummy used to sit in Papa's lap. Does Indian society speak like that or think like that? So, he is gradually losing his balance," he added.During an interaction with students at the University of Chicago in the US, Rahul Gandhi was asked why the opposition does not boycott elections if it believes they were being rigged.The Congress leader said Indian democracy was "sacred" to him and that he would need overwhelming evidence to even claim that it was under threat."Indian democracy is sacred. For me to even say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200, 300 per cent proof," Rahul said."But what happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, 'Okay, don't participate in the election?' If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that minute. And we don't want to end the structure of Indian democracy," he said.Rahul said the opposition's strategy was to highlight alleged electoral irregularities and continue contesting elections until people realise what he claimed was the dismantling of the system."So, our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the beating until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished," he added.BJP has repeatedly criticised Rahul Gandhi over his remarks during foreign visits, accusing him of maligning India and its democratic institutions.The latest controversy comes after Rahul raised allegations of "vote chori" during an earlier interaction at Columbia University, prompting BJP leaders to accuse him of insulting India and its democracy.Rahul was on a two-day visit to the US during which he interacted with students at Columbia University in New York on Tuesday and the University of Chicago on Wednesday.
Article Summary: BJP leaders claim that Rahul Gandhi called Indian democracy "sick" The video put out by news agencies showed that he had actually described the democracy as "sacred" Rahul was on a two-day visit to the US during which he interacted with students at Columbia University in New York and the University of Chicago on Wednesday.

NEW DELHI: The selection of India's playing XI has triggered a face-off between the Congress and the BJP, with the opposition alleging discrimination against pacer Mohammed Siraj and the ruling party accusing it of dragging communal politics into cricket.The exchange began after India’s team management opted for a four-pronged pace attack but left out Siraj against New Zealand, despite the Hyderabad pacer’s impressive record and reputation for delivering in challenging conditions.Congress MP Imran Masood questioned Siraj’s exclusion, suggesting that his religious identity could have played a role in the decision."His name is Siraj -- isn't that reason enough? If he is performing and still not getting selected, what else could be the reason behind it? This alone can be the reason; there can be no other reason besides this," Masood told news agency IANS.In another interaction, the Congress MP said it was being pointed out that Siraj had performed well but was still not included in the team. "If you are not selecting him despite his good performance, the discrimination is clear," he told news agency ANI.The BJP was quick to hit back, accusing the Congress of turning team selection into a communal issue and using cricket for vote-bank politics.BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari said, "Shame on Congress! Congress now does vote bank politics even in Cricket team selection! Congress says - 'Siraj was left out because he was a Muslim'."Pointing out that all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja had also been left out, Bhandari said, "Every cricketer wears the jersey representing India! Stop dividing Indian cricket team for vote bank and communal politics!"Siraj's omission has also drawn attention because of the role he has played in India's pace attack over the past few years.Fifteen months ago, on a cloudy morning in London, Siraj stepped out of Jasprit Bumrah's shadow to produce one of the most memorable performances of his career. The pacer emptied the tank on the final day of a gruelling five-Test series to help India secure a 2-2 draw against England at The Oval.His performance appeared to signal the beginning of a new phase in his career, with Siraj emerging as a potential leader of India's pace attack as Bumrah entered an intensive workload management programme.However, the pacer was left out on Thursday despite conditions in Wellington appearing tailor-made for seam bowling. The team management instead went ahead with four other seamers.One possible reason for the decision could be Siraj's recent form. His underwhelming performance against Sri Lanka in the Colombo Test three months ago may have prompted the team management to reassess his place in the playing XI.
Article Summary: Mohammed Siraj left out of India's pace attack against New Zealand. Congress alleges discrimination, BJP says stop dividing team for vote bank and communal politics. India's team management opted for a four-pronged pace attack but left out Siraj.

Article Title: 'Everybody's got an opinion': Rahul Gandhi explains why he is called a youth leader at 56

Rahul Gandhi at the University of Chicago

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi responded to being called a 'youth leader' despite being 56, saying age should not define youth. In a conversation, Rahul said remaining curious and never being afraid to ask questions, even those considered unusual or ridiculous, was what kept a person young.During a conversation at the University of Chicago, Rahul said he had never accepted the idea that certain questions should not be asked and believed curiosity across subjects was what defined youth."Look, everybody's got an opinion, okay? So somebody will say, I'm a youth leader. Somebody will say, I'm an old people's leader. Somebody will say something else. I mean, it's fine. Everybody is allowed to have a perspective," Rahul said.Responding to a question about why young people identify with him, Rahul Gandhi said he had been encouraged from an early age to remain curious and ask questions across different subjects."But I was taught when I was small to always be curious and to not have boundaries on your curiosity. So to ask questions in all spheres, you know, ask a question about geopolitics, ask a question about women's health, ask a question about animals, ask a question about pretty much anything," he said.He added that society gradually places restrictions on people's curiosity as they grow older, encouraging them to focus on conventional measures of success."So what society is going to try and tell you as you progress is that there are certain questions you can't ask, and there's certain questions that you just shouldn't ask. And there is a set of questions that you can ask," Rahul Gandhi said."You know, you can ask, how do I make money? You can ask, how do I own a big house? You can ask, how do I do well at work as adults? But then there's a whole bunch of questions you're not allowed to ask. I never bought into that."He cited the example of his former mathematics tutor, whom he met for breakfast and learnt was pursuing a master's degree in his 60s.Rahul Gandhi said people should continue asking questions, including those that others might consider unusual or uncomfortable."And to me, that is what you have right now that you should never lose, never be scared of asking the most ridiculous questions, questions that people just will not ask themselves. And that's what youth is. So maybe that's why they say I'm a youth leader," he said.The conversation also turned to generational change in political leadership, particularly in the United States, where younger leaders from different political camps are emerging.Asked about the youth movement in American politics, Rahul Gandhi said he had noticed a shift in how Western leaders approached international affairs. He recalled that leaders he encountered early in his political career had a broader understanding of global developments."I noticed something in leadership in the West. Right. And I noticed when I first came into politics, the leaders had a pretty good understanding of. Of the rest of the world. There was a decent sense. I remember having a conversation with Mr. Tony Blair, and I was like, okay, he gets Afghanistan or he has a sense of India," he said.However, Gandhi said he later encountered leaders who appeared more focused on domestic issues and had limited understanding of developments in other countries."And then suddenly in the middle, I found a group of leaders who were focused completely on what was going on in their country. And they would come, and I'm not saying one particular country, they'd come. And it was obvious that they didn't have the grounding or understanding of our stuff," he said.Rahul Gandhi also referred to Russian President Vladimir Putin while discussing leaders with a broader understanding of geopolitics."At risk of getting into trouble. Mr. Putin has one of the most profound geopolitical minds that I have come across. He can talk in massive sweep about these type of things. And I think that was the thing that. That struck me. There was a moving inwards of Western leadership," he said.He added that Western leaders had increasingly focused on domestic issues rather than developments beyond their borders."you know, looking inside and focusing on the home more than outside. That's just an experience I had. I don't know if I'm correct or wrong," Congress leader said.He also suggested that some younger leaders were beginning to show a wider interest in international affairs."But the reason I said that is that some of these young guys, they seem to be re looking at the outside world. They seem to be having now a vision of a bigger scope than earlier," he said.

NEW DELHI: Faced with a "piquant situation" in deciding a custody battle over a four-year-old child of unwed parents of different nationalities - a Singapore-based German mother who works for TikTok and an Indian father who runs a legal firm in Delhi - SC examined their proposals to care for the child and allowed the mother to take him to Singapore, granting visitation rights to the father.A bench of Justices N K Singh and N V Anjaria said it was seeking to protect the child's autonomy, which had been jeopardised by parents' bickering. After filing it, she must deposit Rs 1 crore with the SC registry, to be kept in a fixed deposit for two years or until the guardianship petition is disposed of.

Article Title: During SCO meet, Purana Qila to open window to 3,000 years ago
Article Text:
(Photo: Anushka Kogta/TNN) A first-of-its kind archaeological experiencepavilion at Purana Qila, which will showcase discoveries at the site and the nearly 3,000-year-old story of Delhi, will be openedto visitors from Monday. SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum will be inaugurated today by PM Narendra Modi at Purana Qila

-

NEW DELHI: Archaeologists and workers carefully scrape away the soil inch by inch to uncover treasures that have been witness to India’s civilisational journey at the iconic Purana Qila complex. An adjoining trench at the excavation site that goes 6.5 metres down reveals eight layers from Mauryan to Mughal period bearing stories of homes that once thrived, the utensils people used, the wood that survived and nuggets of daily life that evolved through India’s many ages.This curated first-of-its-kind archaeological experience pavilion exhibiting a live excavation site and discoveries made at Purana Qila mapping Delhi’s story going back almost 3,000 years will be open to visitors from Monday.Purana Qila, popularly known as Pandavon-ka-Qila, has been identified as the ancient city of Indraprastha, mentioned in the literary work Mahabharata. The standing ramparts and other buildings were built by Sher Shah Suri (1538-1545 CE) after demolishing and re-modeling Dinpanah, a city founded here by Humayun, the sixth city of Delhi, around 1533 CE after his return from Persia.Usually, after excavation a site is filled up with soil but in an attempt to allow people to experience history this exhibition site with the theme "Astitva" - "The Essence Of Our Existence" is being curated to show the layers while ensuring the sanctity of the site is maintained.Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Forum for Civilisational Dialogue on Friday evening at Purana Qila followed by sessions over Saturday and Sunday. The opening ceremony will feature a special program titled “Dialogue of Civilizations— Cultural Performance.” It will feature a unique blend of music, dance, visual storytelling, and narration. Based on the theme Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam—The World is One Family, the presentation will highlight the cultural ties between India and Eurasia. World leaders coming for the Dialogue will get to see the 'Astitva' exhibition which will also be inaugurated on Friday evening.Archaeological Survey of India director Vasant Kumar Swarnkar who has been working at the Purana Qila site since 2013-14 and has led the most recent excavations undertaken in 2022-2023, said the excavations across the complex from the 1950s to date have revealed a nine-fold cultural sequence, beginning with Pre-Mauryan habitations to the Mughal Period, without any breaks.Among the oldest are Sherds of PGW (Painted Grey Ware)– pre-Mauryan levels and these will be part of the experience pavilion that includes the Mauryan Ashvamedha Yagya, ring well and Sunga–Kushana house complex, offering insights into ancient rituals, water management and domestic life.When TOI visited the site on Wednesday, we observed an elevated deck over and around the trenches which will offer visitors a view of the exposed archaeological remains. We explored a space that is likely to have been a room in a house in the Mughal period, a brick platform of Kushan period, rammed floor of Gupta period, pottery pieces from the Rajput period and a kiln from Mauryan era.Equipped with artefact showcases, interpretative panels, the exhibition will highlight to the visitors discoveries ranging from pottery, coins, seals, beads, terracotta figurines, a Kushan period Gajalakshmi terracotta plaque and a Vaikuntha Vishnu stone sculpture from Rajput period—each revealing stories of craftsmanship, trade, beliefs and everyday life.
Article Summary: SCO Civilisation Dialogue Forum will be inaugurated today by PM Narendra Modi at Purana Qila. An adjoining trench at the excavation site that goes 6.5 metres down reveals eight layers from Mauryan to Mughal period bearing stories of homes that once thrived.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Karl-Anthony Towns had a helping hand from an unexpected place in the Knicks’ 102-99 win over the Timberwolves on Thursday night. His father, Karl Towns Sr., pulled him off the floor after an and-1 finish in the first quarter at Target Center in Minneapolis. The 31-year-old big man went on to score 22 points with 12 rebounds. It was the 15th straight double-double to open the season, a new franchise record. New York improved to 9-6 and has won three in a row. Only three points separated the teams at the final buzzer.Karl-Anthony Towns attacked the rim in the first quarter, finished through contact and drew the foul. He hit the floor on the play, and Karl Towns Sr. was close enough to reach down and help him up. The two shared a quick celebration at courtside, and cameras caught it. A clip of the moment was posted on social media.Towns went right at Minnesota inside the paint from the start. The Timberwolves are one of the better teams in the Western Conference, and the and-1 came early. Towns is in a third season with the Knicks and has played in the NBA since 2015. Target Center is an old stomping ground for him, and a family member was right there to see the win.Towns finished with 22 points, 12 rebounds, four assists and three blocks in 32 minutes. He made 9 of 20 shots and 2 of 8 from three, the one soft spot in the line. The rest sits close to the season averages of 21.2 points, 14.1 rebounds and 3.9 assists he took into the game.The Knicks have played 15 games, and Towns has a double-double in every one of them. Rebounding is the biggest piece of what he gives New York on defense. He is not a defensive anchor in the classic sense, but the three blocks helped.Jalen Brunson had an injury scare early, then finished with 21 points and seven assists. New York is defending its championship after a slow start, and the win moved the team to 9-6 and back into the playoff picture. The Knicks rest Friday and host the Portland Trail Blazers at Madison Square Garden on Saturday.

NEW DELHI: Akash Deep's return to Test cricket after a lengthy injury layoff was made more reassuring by the support he received from head coach Gautam Gambhir during rehabilitation. The India fast bowler said Gambhir regularly checked on his progress, and those conversations kept him motivated through a challenging period away from the game.Akash, who had been out of top-flight cricket since August 2025 due to a stress fracture in his back, made an impressive comeback in the first Test against New Zealand, claiming three wickets as India bowled out the visitors for 368 in their first innings.Speaking after the second day's play, the Bengal pacer recalled how Gambhir stayed in touch while he was undergoing rehabilitation at the BCCI Centre of Excellence.“GG (Gambhir) sir used to follow up during that period and he would take updates — ‘Kaisa chal raha?’ he would ask,” Akash said.“Very difficult to come back after a back injury for a fast bowler. Coach was in touch with me during rehab, and it kept motivating me. I worked on skills, and never felt I was away from cricket for this long,” he added.The extended break was not just about regaining fitness. Akash used the time to work on his bowling and improve areas of his game, with his outings for India A also helping him build confidence before returning to the senior side.“During that time, I worked on my bowling and on areas I could improve. I wanted to get stronger. It didn't feel like I was playing international cricket after nearly one and a half years,” he said.“I was happy with what I bowled for India A,” he added.Akash made his comeback count with three for 53 against New Zealand. The dismissal of Glenn Phillips was among the highlights of his spell, as he came wide of the crease and delivered a ball that moved away after pitching to dislodge the batter's off-stump bail.Explaining the delivery, Akash said he had deliberately put in extra effort to generate movement and unsettle the batter.“On that Glenn Phillips wicket delivery, I put in extra effort ki ball zyaada harkat kare. I went wide of the crease to keep batter into play… start playing with batter’s mind,” he said.“It wasn't one (magic) ball. I was trying to bowl in one area. That ball I put in more effort and could get what I wanted to,” he added.The pacer also spoke about the changing conditions at the Basin Reserve, where the pitch had slowed down on the first day before offering some assistance with the new ball on the second.“Yesterday wicket got slower after Lunch, and today there was help with the new ball,” he said.Akash stressed that containing the scoring and sticking to a plan remained important, particularly when bowling with the older ball.“The first option with an old ball is to contain runs and then stick to a plan. My experience here is that you need to bowl to plan and stop the runs. Very difficult to come back after a back injury for a fast bowler,” he said.He also welcomed India's positive batting approach, with openers KL Rahul and Yashasvi Jaiswal putting together a brisk partnership.“We scored quickly and that's a positive sign. Whatever be the opposition, if batters attack like this, bowlers go on the back foot,” Akash said.
Article Summary: Akash had been out of top-flight cricket since August 2025 due to a stress fracture in his back. Article Title: 'They will have to face this': Irfan Pathan predicts Sandpapergate storm for Australia during 2027 Border-Gavaskar Trophy

Former India all-rounder Irfan Pathan believes Australia's fresh ball-tampering scandal revelations could come back to haunt Pat Cummins and his team when they tour India for the Border-Gavaskar Trophy next year. With the controversy back in the spotlight following explosive claims by Usman Khawaja and Cameron Bancroft, Pathan feels the Australian players will face considerable scrutiny from Indian fans and the media.The 2018 ball-tampering scandal, popularly known as 'Sandpapergate', has once again sparked debate after Khawaja and Bancroft suggested that knowledge of the controversial sandpaper tactic extended beyond the players who were directly punished. Their revelations have also raised fresh questions about collective responsibility within the Australian dressing room during the Test series against South Africa.While Cummins dismissed Khawaja's claims as "utter nonsense", Bancroft's detailed account in The West Australian offered further insight into the incident. The opener recalled discussions about reverse swing with Australia's bowlers, including Cummins, and claimed that his actions were encouraged, with several members of the team aware of the plan.Speaking on JioStar, Pathan said the fresh revelations would ensure that Australia remain under the scanner when they arrive in India for the five-match Border-Gavaskar Trophy series in January 2027.Pathan believes the controversy will follow the Australian team throughout their India tour, with Cummins and his teammates needing to be mentally prepared to deal with questions surrounding the scandal."I am pretty sure that when Australia comes down to India to play the BGT series, there will be a lot of talk around it. Wherever the Australians will go, they will have to face this. And they will have to be mentally strong to handle this, because it is all out there in the public domain," Pathan said.Pathan also questioned former Australia opener David Warner's decision to raise concerns about the investigation years after the incident. Warner, along with Steve Smith and Bancroft, was sanctioned following the scandal, with Warner receiving a leadership ban and a lifetime ban from holding a leadership position in Australian cricket.Pathan felt Warner should have spoken up at the time rather than questioning the investigation years later. He also pointed out that Cricket Australia's investigation had identified Warner, who was vice-captain at the time, as the player who initiated the plan to tamper with the ball."I personally believe that Warner, because he has been through a ban, should have spoken then and there. Now, nothing can happen. The investigation happened over four days. Cricket Australia did what they thought was best at that particular time," he said."What I'm assuming from the investigation is that, because David Warner was the vice-captain, he was the one who initiated doing something with the ball. This is what the investigation by Cricket Australia established, and that's why it came out and he was punished."Now, to talk about it and say that it was a shady investigation, I think it is too late. He should have spoken then and there, and things would have been very different," Pathan added.

Article Title: Florida biologist Ian Bartoszek uses 40 radio-tagged male pythons as scout snakes to find breeding females, and his team pulled a record 8,080 pounds of invasive Burmese pythons out of Southwest Flori
Article Text:
PC: Conservancy/Florida's Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences

How 40 radio-tagged male pythons help Florida biologist find breeding females

Florida team removes record 8,080 pounds of pythons

Florida team removes 4,100 Burmese python eggs in record season

Burmese python population spreads to another Florida county

Florida biologist Ian Bartoszek and his team are using 40 radio-tagged male Burmese pythons as “scout snakes” to locate breeding females, helping remove a record 8,080 pounds of invasive pythons from Southwest Florida in a single season. The Conservancy of Southwest Florida said its team removed 177 pythons between November 2025 and April 2026, the highest seasonal removal by weight since its programme began in 2013. The tagged males help researchers track down large females before they lay eggs. The team also removed 4,100 python eggs during the season as part of its efforts to suppress the invasive population and protect native wildlife.According to the Conservancy, its science team uses 40 radio-tagged male Burmese pythons to locate breeding snakes during the mating season. Researchers track the males using radio telemetry, following their movements through the landscape to locate female pythons they are mating with. This allows biologists to capture the females before they lay eggs.The programme uses the tagged males as tracking tools rather than relying solely on searching for pythons directly. The Conservancy said the scout snakes helped its team locate large breeding females deep in the landscape during the latest season.The approach is part of its long-term research and removal programme, which has been operating since 2013.The Conservancy of Southwest Florida said its team removed 177 invasive Burmese pythons weighing a combined 8,080 pounds during the November 2025 to April 2026 breeding season. The organisation described this as the greatest biomass of pythons removed in a single season by its tracking team and volunteers since the programme began.The removed female pythons weighed an average of 95 pounds, while the largest female captured during the season weighed 153 pounds and measured 17 feet long. The Conservancy said the females carried an average of 70 eggs, and a quarter of them contained the remains of white-tailed deer.The team also removed an additional 4,100 Burmese python eggs from the ecosystem during the season. The Conservancy said the removal effort was intended to prevent the eggs from hatching and adding more invasive snakes to the landscape.“This was our first four-ton removal season. Our tagged scout snakes helped us locate large breeding snakes deep in the landscape before they had a chance to lay eggs,” Ian Bartoszek, wildlife biologist and Conservancy Science Project Manager, said. He added that the science-based management efforts were suppressing local python reproduction and that the organisation hoped removal numbers would decline over time with continued pressure.Since 2013, the Conservancy's python research and removal programme has removed 1,750 pythons weighing more than 53,000 pounds from Southwest Florida. The programme has also contributed to 25 collaborative scientific publications examining Burmese python biology and behaviour. Its research involves collaboration with Rookery Bay National Estuarine Research Reserve, the US Geological Survey, the University of Florida and the South Florida Water Management District.Burmese pythons are invasive predators in Florida, and efforts to remove them are aimed at reducing their impact on native wildlife. In a separate October 2026 report, the University of Florida's Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences (UF/IFAS) said an established Burmese python population was also present in Charlotte County, where authorities suspect the snakes initially escaped or were released from captivity. Residents are encouraged to report sightings to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) through the IveGot1 app or its invasive species hotline.
Article Summary: The Conservancy of Southwest Florida said its team removed 177 invasive Burmese pythons weighing a combined 8,080 pounds during the November 2025 to April 2026 breeding season. The team also removed 4,100 python eggs during the season as part of its efforts to suppress the invasive population and protect native wildlife. Researchers track the males using radio telemetry, following their movements through the landscape.

Article Title: 'Liverpool or any other club not involved': Drone operator deletes Mauricio Pochettino's first Man United session's leaked footage

Mauricio Pochettino

Why did the drone operator apologise?

NEW DELHI: Manchester United 's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino came under unexpected attention after footage of his first training session at the club was leaked online.A drone operator filmed around 12 minutes of United's training session at Carrington on Thursday, capturing Pochettino working with his players as they prepared for Sunday's Premier League clash against Liverpool at Anfield.The video showed the Argentine coach conducting training drills and speaking to players in a group huddle. It also offered glimpses of senior players, including Harry Maguire and Bruno Fernandes.Although the drone operator initially defended the recording, claiming the flight followed legal requirements, he later admitted that filming a private training session was inappropriate and removed the video from his YouTube channel.The footage was uploaded to a YouTube channel called CC Overview, run by a man who identified himself as Colin. He mainly shared drone videos of construction work at football stadiums and other events. Following criticism, he accepted that recording United's training session was a mistake.In his apology, he, as quoted by Sky Sports, said, "A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part."He explained that his intention was to capture Pochettino in his new United training kit for supporters. He also admitted that he had wrongly assumed the session had not properly started and that the media had permission to film it.Colin apologised to the club, manager and players, adding, "I would also like to state that Liverpool Football Club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday.The video has been removed from my channel."No. Although Colin deleted the original video, it had already circulated widely across social media platforms, including YouTube, X, Instagram and TikTok.The incident came at an important time for United. Pochettino had replaced Michael Carrick, who was dismissed the previous week after the club dropped to 18th place in the league following its worst start in 40 years.His first major challenge was Sunday's meeting with Liverpool, making the leaked footage an unwelcome distraction ahead of the game.

Article Title: India, Malaysia begin Harimau Shakti military drill with focus on counter-terror ops
Article Text:
Indian Army contingent in Malaysia for Exercise Hiramau Shakti. (Image credit: Indian Army)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The sixth edition of the India-Malaysia joint military exercise Harimau Shakti began on Friday at Ipoh in Malaysia, with 120 personnel from each side taking part. The exercise, a bilateral training event held alternately in the two countries, will run till November 30.The stated aim is to rehearse sub-conventional operations under Chapter VII of the United Nations mandate, with particular emphasis on synergising responses during counter-terrorism missions. The two armies will work in jungle and semi-urban terrain, relying on joint planning, tactical coordination and emerging technologies to improve interoperability.The exercise will unfold in phases. In the first phase, troops will first undergo cross-training to familiarise themselves with each other's operating procedures, followed by joint tactical drills. These include setting up a Joint Command Post and Surveillance Centre, counter-terrorism operations, raids, cordon-and-search drills and combat engineering tasks. Special attention will go to Unmanned Aerial Systems for reconnaissance and surveillance, along with counter-drone capabilities to detect and neutralise hostile unmanned platforms. The exercise will end with a validation drill built around a simulated counter-terrorism scenario, combining ground operations, integrated surveillance and unmanned systems.The fifth edition was held last year at the Mahajan Field Firing Range in Rajasthan from December 5 to 18 last year. The Indian contingent then largely comprised troops from the Dogra Regiment, while Malaysia was represented by the 25th Battalion of the Royal Malaysian Army.The exercise reflects a wider deepening of defence ties. India and Malaysia established diplomatic relations in 1957 and a Memorandum of Understanding on Defence Cooperation signed in 1993 gave military engagement an institutional framework. The Joint Defence Cooperation Committee reviews existing cooperation and identifies new areas. In August 2024, the two countries elevated their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.The naval dimension has grown as well. The fourth edition of Samudra Laksamana was held at Lumut from September 9 to 12 this year, with INS Mysore exercising alongside the Royal Malaysian Navy's KD Lekir and KD Gagah Samudera.In October 2025 INS Sahyadri visited Kemaman, while the survey vessel INS Sandhayak made a port call at Klang in July 2025. The navies of both nations also take part in multilateral platforms such as MILAN and the ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise.Defence manufacturing is emerging as another area of cooperation. India is looking to expand exports to Southeast Asia, while Malaysia seeks to modernise its forces and diversify its sources of procurement. Hindustan Aeronautics Limited, Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders, Bharat Dynamics Limited and BEML showcased their products at LIMA 2025. The two countries are also co-chairing the SEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM) counter-terrorism working group for 2024-2027.
Article Summary: The sixth edition of the India-Malaysia joint military exercise Harimau Shakti began on Friday at Ipoh in Malaysia. The exercise, a bilateral training event held alternately in the two countries, will run till November 30. The stated aim is to rehearse sub-conventional operations under Chapter VII of the United Nations mandate.

Article Title: Chennai techie travelled nearly 2,100km to meet influencer about to get married in Delhi, lost his life
Article Text:
(AI image) A techie named Abhinav died after being allegedly assaulted in east Delhi's Madhu Vihar.





NEW DELHI: The investigation into the death of a techie, who was allegedly beaten up by the father and a neighbour of a woman social media influencer in east Delhi ’s Madhu Vihar on Nov 7, has revealed that he had been allegedly infatuated with her and travelled nearly 2,100 km from Chennai to meet her after learning about her impending marriage.As reported by TOI Thursday, two people, including the woman’s father and the neighbour, were arrested in connection with the incident. Police registered two FIRs, one on the influencer’s complaint alleging trespassing by the techie, Abhinav , and the other in connection with the fatal assault on him.The second complaint had initially been registered on charges of voluntarily causing grievous hurt and common intention, but Section 105 of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), pertaining to culpable homicide not amounting to murder, was subsequently added after his death.The probe has found no evidence of any prior acquaintance between the man and the woman.Abhinav, a native of Uttar Pradesh, used to work with an IT firm in Chennai. The influencer, who has over two million followers, told police that she had been receiving persistent messages from anonymous Instagram accounts, including comments about her daily routine and personal life. She said she initially ignored them as she was accustomed to receiving such messages.According to her complaint, the man had allegedly been trying to contact her for several months.She further told police that she got engaged on June 22 this year and announced it on her social media platforms. Soon after, she allegedly began receiving messages from an Instagram account that had been contacting her for a long time and posting inappropriate comments.She alleged that on July 10-11, an unidentified man entered her house and created a scene, shouting, “I love you, madam. Don’t get married to anyone else.” Her family members and neighbours tried to reason with him. The man allegedly apologised and promised not to repeat the behaviour or contact her again. She did not file a police complaint at the time.The woman claimed that although messages from that particular account stopped subsequently, she continued receiving messages from other anonymous Instagram accounts, which she chose to ignore.According to her complaint to police, her marriage was scheduled for this Dec, an information she shared on social media. On Nov 7, the man allegedly entered her house again and began shouting her name. She recognised him as the same person who had created a disturbance in July, she told police.She alleged that the man was heavily intoxicated and unable to stand properly. When her father questioned him about his presence, he allegedly misbehaved with the family and assaulted her father, saying he would not allow her to marry anyone else.Her neighbours intervened and tried to remove him from the premises. During the altercation, he allegedly fell on the roadside twice or thrice. The influencer claimed he sustained a head injury after falling down and denied that her father or the neighbour was responsible for causing it.Abhinav died on Nov 14. Police arrested the influencer’s father and the neighbour in connection with the case. Further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A techie named Abhinav died after being allegedly assaulted in east Delhi's Madhu Vihar. Two people, including the woman’s father and the neighbour, were arrested in connection with the incident. The influencer, who has over two million followers, told police that she had been receiving persistent messages from anonymous Instagram accounts.

Article Title: 'Address: Tihar Jail, work: To Kill': How D-Company-linked gangster Naseem Durrani's long run ended in UP
Article Text:
Image Credit: TOI/ Special arrangement

How the net closed in

A chequered history





NEW DELHI: For years, Naseem Durrani moved between the gritty turf wars of northeast Delhi and the far-reaching shadow of Mumbai’s underworld — a man whose criminal ledger stretched from neighborhood extortion rackets to alleged hit contracts tied to Dawood Ibrahim ’s "D-Company."Beyond his crimes on the ground, Naseem actively used social media to cultivate a climate of fear among people. His Instagram profile served as an overt display of intimidation, featuring a bio that read: "Name: Badnaam (Notorious) | Address: Tihar Jail | Age: To live | Work: To kill." Through this digital persona, he openly advertised his criminal background while remaining absconding from law enforcement.On Friday, that long run ended in a hail of gunfire in Uttar Pradesh’s Bulandshahr district, where a joint operation by the Noida Special Task Force (STF) and Delhi Police cornered and killed the wanted gangster.Acting on intelligence inputs tracking Durrani’s movements, Delhi crime branch team led by DCP Sanjeev Yadav and deputy superintendent of police R K Mishra from STF Noida mounted a coordinated operation in Bulandshahr, supervised by special CP HGS Dhaliwal.In the early hours, the cops detected his movement near the Sikandra Bypass. CCTV footage showed him riding a scooter, and when the police team moved in to arrest him, he repeatedly looked back at the pursuing officers while speeding away.​During the chase, Naseem's scooter skidded and fell. Armed with two .32-bore pistols, he opened fire on the police team, prompting officers to retaliate. He sustained multiple gunshot wounds in the exchange of fire, and police recovered both pistols from the spot.The breakthrough came days after a brazen daylight-style shooting in northeast Delhi put law enforcement on high alert. Investigators had been scanning CCTV footage, tracing escape routes, and following leads in the wake of a deadly attack in Khajuri Khas.While police files linked Durrani to more than 25 criminal cases — spanning murder, attempt to murder, and robbery — his profile extended well beyond local street crime. The first was a killing outside Delhi law minister Kapil Mishra's camp office where 26-year-old Sameer was shot dead with over a dozen rounds fired in the attack.Police scrutiny following the recent violence has pointed to a prolonged gang feud in northeast Delhi, allegedly driven by extortion demands targeting shared auto-rickshaw operators and scrap dealers. Durrani had also previously been named as a key accused in the May 26 killing of Raja Mewati, alias "Akki Don," in Khajuri Khas.Investigators noted that Durrani had links to Dawood Ibrahim’s D-Company and remained in contact with underworld figure Chhota Shakeel. According to reports, Shakeel had allegedly handed Durrani a contract during 2016–2017 to eliminate rival gangster Chhota Rajan, who was lodged in Tihar Jail.With Durrani killed in the Bulandshahr encounter, investigators are expected to examine how his network operated across the Delhi-NCR and western Uttar Pradesh belt, as well as any lingering fallout from the ongoing turf wars in northeast Delhi.
Article Summary: Gangster Naseem Durrani was shot dead by police in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh. He was wanted in more than 25 criminal cases spanning murder, attempt to murder, and robbery. His criminal ledger stretched from neighborhood extortion rackets to alleged hit contracts tied to Dawood Ibrahim’s "D-Company"

Article Title: As Cambridge Dictionary picks ‘human' as word of the year 2026, Bill Gates says, 'I believe AI has the...'
Article Text:
Bill Gates reacts as Cambridge Dictionary picks ‘human' as word of the year 3026

Why Cambridge Dictionary named ‘human’ as word of the year 2026

“The year was defined by global debates on what it means to be human when AI is blurring the boundaries between people and machines.

In 2016, many public figures defended humans and humanity in the age of AI. Bill Gates made the case for “human reserved jobs”, such as caregivers, that should never be taken by machines, in a widely read essay.

Throughout history, the adjective human has signified people, as opposed to animals and gods (and, more recently, machines). Increasingly seen in compounds such as human-written, human-generated, and human-made, it now also denotes that something is created by or typical of people as opposed to AI .

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

It’s possible that this shift is simply a natural linguistic development, reflecting the ubiquity of AI, but it could be evidence of something more interesting: a turning point in our attitude towards

artificial intelligence

.

When we look back on 2026 in years to come, it might prove to have been a pivotal moment in the story of human versus machine.

In May of this year, the University of California, San Diego, published a landmark study which for the first time revealed empirical evidence for artificial intelligence systems passing the Turing Test. In 73 percent of cases, after a 15-minute text conversation, GPT-4.5 was judged to be ‘human’.

We have now reached a point where AI can produce writing, art, and music that can pass for human-made content. Some people are even questioning whether AI has achieved sentience. This gives rise to some profound existential questions. What are the implications for humanity? What does it even mean to be human in the age of AI?"

Cambridge University recently named ‘human’ as the Word of the Year 2026, a choice that caught the attention of Microsoft founder Bill Gates. Reacting to the Cambridge University announcement, Bill Gates said he believes AI has the potential to cure diseases, improve education and give people more time for what matters most. However, he also stressed the need to make deliberate choices about how AI fits into our lives and where humans should remain at the centre. “Cambridge Dictionary just picked “human” as its Word of the Year. The measure of AI’s success should be how much it improves lives, so I can’t think of a better choice for this moment,” Gates wrote in an X post.“I believe AI has the potential to cure diseases, improve education, and give people more time to spend on the things that matter most. Article Title: As Anthropic makes its Wall Street debut, CEO Dario Amodei says ‘We will not bend to either business or political pressure’
Article Text:
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

Here’s what CEO Dario Amodei said on Anthropic IPO

"My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind.

Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that, just a few years later, became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments.

So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket—tools for gene editing, gene synthesis, controlling brain cells with light—started as pure ideas.

In other words, they came from thinking. From intelligence.

Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress on other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades: it took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR.

Nature is full of these patterns. But we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them; too few scientists, with too little time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would’ve taken just a couple of years ago.

I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.

I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time. And although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe those processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by just a few years.

Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many others. Our customers—the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people—are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth; lift people out of poverty; protect democracy and free societies; even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them. And I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future.

At the same time, we have always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or nation-states, to economic disruption, to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable, but because we think they are avoidable.

Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety, versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety.

And an obsession with safety and with public benefit has been woven into Anthropic’s DNA from the start. From safeguards against biological and cyber risks, to alignment training and testing, to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI systems.

There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us. The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed, even more so than it has already, towards double- and triple-checking that those AI systems are safe and secure.

And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure. Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing.

If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same.

We call this a race to the top. When the race to the top is working properly, it doesn’t matter which company has the best models—everyone wins because everyone is building safely. The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.

The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history, and we have a rare opportunity to shape it for the better.

This moment is bigger than any one company, or any one country. It will take all of us, working together, to ensure this technology goes well for us and the many generations to come. Starting today, we hope that you’ll join us on this mission."

Claude-maker Anthropic made its blockbuster debut on Wall Street with the company’s valuation reaching nearly $2 trillion. Shares of the company closed at $97.17, up by 17% from its IPO price of $83. Soon after the debut, Anthropic shared a statement from CEO Dario Amodei reaffirming the company’s core focus on safety, committing to pace AI training and deployment as needed to maintain human control while resisting business or political pressures, framing this as essential to avoid risks like misuse or loss of control. “Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” Amodei said.“If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top,” he added.
