Article Title: Microsoft staff wrote open letter that they fear being replaced by AI, then 60,000 got exit offers; Satya Nadella now says: Why do we need software engineers? To...
Article Text:
​What Nadella sees next for every Microsoft job​​

Nadella says every job at Microsoft will turn into managing AI agents

Microsoft employees had already put their AI worries in writing

Microsoft’s 60,000 buyout offer covers teams in India, US, Canada and UK

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has given his clearest explanation yet for why the company asked around 60,000 employees, more than a quarter of its workforce, to consider leaving. Speaking to Andrew Ross Sorkin at the NYT DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Nadella said the buyout was meant “to make sure that at least everyone felt like they had agency in making choices” as Microsoft rebuilds itself around AI. His comments come weeks after a group of Microsoft workers circulated an open letter. It accused the company of chasing AI with a “speed-at-all-costs” ethos and flagged “threats of AI job replacement and layoffs.”Nadella made it clear that the plan is not to swap engineers for AI.“Let’s take software engineering. We went from, ‘Well, we don’t buy that AI can ever do software.’ To suddenly, ‘Wow, it can do all software, and why do we need software engineers?’ To now rediscovering that software engineering is very much alive and, in fact, is going to thrive, except the way the team is organized and the work that a software engineer does has now got a new operating point,” he said.Some people, he admitted, find “that reorganization and change is sort of hard,” but “it has to be done.”To show what that new operating point looks like, Nadella pointed to the team behind Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps. The team has just 11 developers, and they have learnt to let AI do most of the building. “They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product,” he said.He expects every employee to eventually direct AI agents instead of doing the work themselves.“That level of direction is what, by the way, is going to happen in all jobs,” Nadella said. He also admitted that a 51-year-old company was not born AI-first, and that the shift “is going to take a bit more time than anyone expects.”On a podcast with Gergely Orosz last week, he went a step further. He said the industry had “created enormous anxiety” among workers with talk of the singularity and of AI taking away all jobs.Before the buyouts were announced, current and former employees circulated a letter signed “Concerned Microsoft Workers.” It called working at the company “joyless and demoralizing.” According to the letter, staff were pushed to use AI in almost every area with little training, and were spending time “fixing AI slop” and reworking low-quality features.The letter asked Microsoft to involve workers in decisions on AI and to stop tying AI use to rewards, reprimands or layoffs. It also asked the company to treat AI as an assistive tool rather than “a complete labor replacement.”Six employees told the NYT that the buyout landed on a workforce already strained by AI targets and stagnant pay, with some merit raises this year below 1%. Gretchen Thomas, a design leader who left in September, had her stock award cut. According to a memo seen by the NYT, part of the reason was that she did “not consistently” show speed, urgency and willingness to experiment, including with AI.Microsoft confirmed the Voluntary Exit Offer on October 26. It covers employees at vice president level and below on select teams in the US, Canada, India and the UK. Xbox, Windows, Copilot and Finance are among the divisions involved.Employees have until December 9 to decide, and those who accept will leave on December 31 with at least eight weeks of base pay. Microsoft expects fewer than 5% to take it. This is its second buyout this year, after a retirement-age offer earlier in 2026. It also follows layoffs of 10,000 people in 2023, over 15,000 in 2025 and about 4,800 this summer.Chief people officer Amy Coleman told the NYT that the buyouts were not linked to how AI is changing work, and she did not rule out future layoffs. Two days after the offer, Microsoft reported quarterly profit of $36.6 billion, up 32%. Capital spending, mostly on data centres, rose 30% to $45.2 billion, and the company expects to spend roughly $170 billion this year.For those who stay, the worry is more immediate. Employees told the NYT they do not expect departing colleagues to be replaced, so their work will land on the people left behind. That is where Nadella’s new operating point will be tested first.
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says every job at the company will turn into managing AI agents. He made it clear that the plan is not to swap engineers for AI. Microsoft confirmed the Voluntary Exit Offer on October 26. It covers employees at vice president level and below on select teams in US, Canada, India and UK.

Article Title: Missing for 5 years, found in Rajasthan: How AI helped UP cops trace woman using childhood photo
Article Text:
In photos: The missing woman in the original photograph and her AI-generated image





LUCKNOW: In an unusual use of artificial intelligence in a police investigation, Sonbhadra Police traced and safely recovered a 35-year-old woman who had been missing for nearly five years after generating a probable image of her present-day appearance using AI tools, as investigators did not have access to a recent photograph.The woman, a resident of the Babhani police station area, had been missing since 2021. Investigators faced a major challenge in tracing her as her family did not have a single recent photograph that could help identify her after all these years.SP (Operations) Rishabh Runwal said that during the investigation, the police team found a scholarship application form dating back to 2007 at the woman's former school. The form contained a photograph of her taken when she was studying in Class IV, providing investigators with their only available visual reference."Constable Vijay Pandey used the childhood photograph, along with pictures of the woman's parents and sister, to generate a probable image of her present-day appearance with the assistance of ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The AI-generated image was subsequently shown to her family members, who recognised her," Runwal said.He further added that, using the image as a lead and information gathered during the investigation, Constable Pandey traced the woman to Churu district in Rajasthan and successfully recovered her."The operation highlighted how AI tools can supplement conventional police investigations, particularly in cases where investigators lack updated photographs or other crucial identification material. However, the breakthrough was made possible by the constable's sustained efforts, field investigation and follow-up on leads," Sonbhadra SP Abhishek Verma said.Recognising his efforts, Sonbhadra Superintendent of Police awarded Constable Vijay Pandey a commendation certificate and a cash reward of Rs 2,100 on Friday.The case demonstrates how emerging technology, when combined with traditional intelligence gathering and persistent police work, can help overcome investigative challenges in long-pending missing-person cases, SP Verma added.

Investigators faced a major challenge in tracing her as her family did not have a single recent photograph that could help identify her. The police team found a scholarship application form dating back to 2007 at the woman's former school. It contained a photograph of her taken when she was studying in Class IV, providing investigators with their only available visual reference.

Article Title: Happy birthday, then goodbye: English club sacks struggling manager hours after publicly wishing him a happy 45th birthday
Article Text:
Blackpool sack Ian Evatt hours after wishing him happy 45th birthday

Blackpool sack Ian Evatt hours after birthday tribute

Poor League One form brings Evatt's second spell to an end

Ian Evatt's playing history at Blackpool and return as manager

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Blackpool have dismissed Ian Evatt as head coach less than seven hours after publicly wishing him a happy 45th birthday, bringing an abrupt end to his 12-month return to Bloomfield Road. The timing of the announcement attracted immediate attention, but the decision followed a difficult run of results that had left the League One club hovering just above the relegation places. Evatt's final match was a 1-0 defeat against AFC Wimbledon.Blackpool announced Evatt's departure on Thursday, November 19, 2026, just hours after posting a birthday message for the former defender on the club's official social media accounts. The 45-year-old had returned to Bloomfield Road in October 2025, but his tenure ended after 12 months as the club moved to make a change during a difficult period in League One.The club confirmed the decision in a brief statement, thanking Evatt for his work and naming the coaching staff who would oversee the team for their next fixture."Blackpool Football Club can announce that Ian Evatt has departed his role as Head Coach after 12 months in charge.The Club thanks Ian for all of his efforts during his time at Bloomfield Road. Steve Thompson will take charge of the team for this weekend’s fixture, along with Stephen Crainey, Stephen Dobbie and Steve Banks."Steve Thompson will therefore lead the side against Wigan Athletic on Saturday, November 21, alongside Crainey, Dobbie and Banks, as Blackpool begin their search for a permanent successor.The timing of the dismissal made headlines, but Blackpool's recent results had placed Evatt under increasing pressure. The Seasiders had lost six of their previous 10 league matches, leaving them only just above the League One relegation zone and struggling to build consistency.His final game was a 1-0 defeat away to AFC Wimbledon. Evatt had explained before the match that a sickness bug had disrupted preparations and affected several players, limiting his options for the trip to London. The defeat nevertheless extended the club's poor run and proved to be his last in charge.Evatt's 12 months at Bloomfield Road included an initial period of improvement, particularly during a strong run in December that helped move Blackpool away from immediate danger. However, that momentum proved difficult to sustain. Injuries repeatedly disrupted his selection, with defensive absences particularly troublesome, and he struggled to establish a settled side across 57 matches in charge.Blackpool now face the task of finding a manager who can stabilise their league position and improve performances during the winter schedule. The club's next fixture against Wigan will be the first under Thompson's interim leadership.Evatt's departure is notable given his previous standing at the club as a player. He joined Blackpool on loan from Queens Park Rangers in 2006, made the move permanent in 2007 and remained at Bloomfield Road until 2013, making more than 250 appearances as a centre-back.He was an important part of the side that climbed from League One to the Premier League, helping Blackpool secure promotion in 2006-07 and again in 2009-10 through successful play-off campaigns. The latter achievement took the club into the Premier League for the 2010-11 season, a landmark period in its modern history.His playing career had made him a familiar figure to Blackpool supporters long before he returned as head coach. Appointed in October 2025 as successor to Steve Bruce, Evatt was tasked with improving the club's position and building a more competitive side. His second spell, however, lasted only 12 months.The dismissal also marks another managerial change under owner Simon Sadler, who took control of Blackpool in 2019. Evatt's departure represents the club's eighth permanent managerial appointment during Sadler's ownership, with the board once again looking for someone capable of delivering greater consistency.
Article Summary: Blackpool sack Ian Evatt hours after wishing him happy 45th birthday. The 45-year-old had returned to Bloomfield Road in October 2025. His tenure ended after 12 months as the club moved to make a change. The decision followed a difficult run of results that had left the League One club hovering just above the relegation places.

Article Title: Decoding wedding dress codes and bizarre themes
Article Text:
What was once a wedding invitation now comes with what looks like a fashion assignment





Dressing up for a wedding and picking an appropriate sari, lehenga or a salwar kameez of your choice was supposed to be an exciting experience. Somehow, dressing up for an upscale Delhi wedding has turned into an exercise that requires a fair understanding of fashion terms, Bollywood wedding trends and, of course, a certain budget for your ‘wedding wardrobe’. Add to this the confusion of receiving a wedding invite that lists Carnival Chic, Tropical Disco, Modern Royals, Boho Chic, Garden Party or Surrealist Ball as dress codes for different functions. One needs a consultation with fashion experts and a bit of reading to decode these themes! And just when you think you have figured out Carnival Chic, another function expects you to turn up looking like a Modern Royal. In some cases, one might get lucky and receive a mood board or Pinterest inspiration from hosts trying their best to ensure guests comply with the dress codes. What was once a wedding invitation now comes with what looks like a fashion assignment.While hosts may spend months planning these themes and want their carefully choreographed wedding moments and aesthetic shots to go just right, for guests, it means a wardrobe makeover they never asked for. Most weddings today have multiple functions, each with its own theme and dress code. The beautiful sari bought for the sangeet may not make the cut for the cocktail, and the mehendi outfit certainly won’t do for the wedding.What follows is a shopping spree, an added expense and a lot of effort to put together outfits that will probably lie hidden in your wardrobe for years after being worn just once. And that’s assuming you have managed to find something that fits the theme in the first place.It is not just dress code themes that have become more complicated, but also the colour palettes. You may have a pink sari, but will it qualify if the dress code says dusty rose? Will your green kurta work for a pistachio or sage green theme? Is black appropriate if the theme specifies charcoal? And do you even know what shade champagne is? Of course, one has the choice to go with their own understanding and interpretation of these themes, but no one wants to look like the odd one out at an event where everyone else is dressed as a supporting character in a Bollywood shaadi sequence. And if you happen to be among the close group of the bride or groom, turning up in the wrong shade could lead to disagreements that might take longer to settle than the wedding itself.Attending luxury, fancy weddings sure sounds like a lot of fun, but remember that it comes with its own set of complications. So before you commit to any such wedding this season, ensure you are well versed with the fashion brief for the wedding wardrobe of the season and have kept aside a shopping budget that may exceed your own expectations. And perhaps, while sending out the invitation, hosts could also consider adding a fashion consultant’s number alongside the wedding planners. After all, if guests are expected to follow a dress code for every function, a little help in decoding it wouldn’t hurt.
Article Summary: Dressing up for an upscale Delhi wedding has turned into an exercise that requires a fair understanding of fashion terms and Bollywood wedding trends. Add to this the confusion of receiving a wedding invite that lists Carnival Chic, Tropical Disco, Modern Royals, Boho Chic, Garden Party or Surrealist Ball as dress codes.
